message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Publish NuGet package

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  release:
    branches: [ master ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      with: 
        submodules: true
        fetch-depth: 0
    - name: Cache NuGet packages
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.nuget/packages
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-${{ hashFiles('**/*.csproj', '**/packages.lock.json') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-nuget-
    - name: Publish NuGet package
      working-directory: src
      run: |
          git submodule update --force --recursive --init --remote
          dotnet restore
          dotnet build --configuration Release
          dotnet pack ./ACadSharp/ACadSharp.csproj --configuration Release
          foreach($file in (Get-ChildItem ./nupkg -Recurse -Include *.nupkg)) {
               dotnet nuget push $file --api-key "${{ secrets.NUGET_API_KEY }}" --source https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json --skip-duplicate
          }",
  "rationale": "The workflow runs `dotnet restore` on every release/dispatch, repeatedly downloading NuGet dependencies. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern (dependency_cache; reported VM-time reduction 6% free / 3.4% paid, Table 4) supports caching dependency downloads when lockfile/environment inputs are keyed and no equivalent cache exists. Add an `actions/cache` step for the NuGet global packages folder (`~/.nuget/packages`) keyed on `**/*.csproj` and `**/packages.lock.json` before `dotnet restore`. All build, pack, and push steps are preserved; no permissions, secrets, or deployment operations are changed.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
